title: Pre-Analysis — Oceanic Clearance and Surveillance Extension of the Router Standard
abstract: Closed re-analysis of the second router standard, run to extend its retrofit effectivity to a third operator, covering the antenna land condition that made the prerequisite inspection necessary and the crew content that had lagged the change.

sections.objective: Support an effectivity extension of the second router standard to a third operator's fleet, and establish why the first ten upgrades produced five antenna land findings when the design had assumed none.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. The decisive one was the antenna land: four of the first ten aircraft had degraded sealant and one had a bonding resistance outside limits, on lands that had never been opened since delivery. The analysis could not show that the land condition was predictable from build standard or from operating environment, so the prerequisite inspection was retained rather than deleted as the extension request had asked. The second finding was that the surveillance report test had been treated as part of the log-on test rather than as a separate acceptance step, which meant the first embodiments had no recorded evidence that surveillance worked. The remaining two were content items on the wiring schematic and the crew description, both of which still described the first standard.
sections.next_steps: Keep the prerequisite inspection in the effectivity extension and say why in the planning information. Separate the surveillance report test as its own acceptance step at the next bulletin revision. Re-issue the wiring schematic with the second concentrator position shown. Hand the crew description update to the flight operations office as a separate action.

similarity_seeds: sealant and bonding condition at an antenna land that has never been opened

tasks.title: Analyse the first ten embodiment findings
Search structural practice covering antenna land preparation

expected_findings.rationale: The prerequisite inspection was raised after the first ten upgrades and the extension request asked for it to be deleted. The analysis could not show that the land condition is predictable from build standard or environment, so it was retained.
expected_findings.resolution: Prerequisite retained in the effectivity extension with the reasoning recorded in the planning information.

evidence.similarity_note: Connected only by the subject of preparing and protecting a metallic land; no identifier is common to the two documents.

expected_findings.rationale: Where a land was found outside limits the repair scheme applied was written for a structural land rather than for a bonded electrical interface, and the two have different acceptance criteria.
expected_findings.resolution: Cross-reference added between the bulletin and the repair scheme.

expected_findings.rationale: The schematic still showed a single data concentrator and had not been re-drawn for the second position, which meant the sheet did not match any upgraded aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Sheet re-issued with the second concentrator position and the satellite antenna feed shown.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew description and the modification share no identifier and almost no vocabulary; the link is the log-on behaviour that both describe from different sides.

expected_findings.rationale: The crew description still described the log-on behaviour of the first standard, in which a failed log-on was annunciated immediately rather than after three automatic retries.
expected_findings.resolution: Handed to the flight operations office as a separate action and issued with the following revision.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned first by every entity search because it is the predecessor and shares four part numbers. It was already fully understood and was not a finding of this analysis; the work was about the second standard's own effectivity.

type_data.conclusion: Effectivity extension approved with the prerequisite inspection retained. Surveillance report test separated as its own acceptance step.
